concept: Partition Field Cardinality and the 2023-06-07 Storage Engine Change
summary: Source-anchored research for Partition Field Cardinality and the 2023-06-07 Storage Engine Change. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: A May 2023 user reported archival progress stopping near 2.03 GB while CPU rose, using a high-cardinality integer timestamp and string user ID. MongoDB support discouraged high-cardinality string keys and suggested testing without them. This thread supplies a diagnostic lead, not a measured root-cause finding or a universal size threshold. (low confidence)

The documented high-cardinality restriction concerns string fields on older Online Archives: many distinct string values create many partitions. Current configuration documentation says this warning does not apply to archives created after June 2023; a May 25, 2023 community reply links allowing high-cardinality strings to the forthcoming backend storage change. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

A MongoDB-authored article preserved in its Hugging Face dataset gives an unqualified warning against high-cardinality fields such as _id because many object-storage partitions can slow aggregation queries. Treat that preserved text as legacy guidance requiring the archive-generation qualification in current configuration documentation. (medium confidence)

MongoDB's June 13, 2023 launch announcement says the new features initially applied to Online Archives created on or after June 7, 2023. The cutoff is inclusive and concerns archive creation, rather than document age or a MongoDB server version. (high confidence)

The configuration documentation recommends explain to inspect partitions used by an archive query. Use that diagnostic to evaluate candidate partition fields against actual query predicates instead of assuming cardinality alone determines the amount scanned. (low confidence)

MongoDB describes the new Online Archive storage engine as capturing metadata during archival to reduce data scanned by queries, with sorting and ongoing rebalancing as additional optimizations. The announcement provides no quantitative speedup or cardinality threshold. (medium confidence)

For partition selection, MongoDB recommends fields frequently used in archive queries. Davi Orlandi's practitioner article likewise starts from real historical queries and recommends moderate cardinality; accepting high-cardinality strings does not establish that every such field is beneficial for every query workload. (high confidence)

At launch, archives created before June 7, 2023 continued operating without the new enhancements. MongoDB announced an intention to migrate existing archives over the coming year; that statement is a historical plan, not confirmation of completed migration. (low confidence)

Joe Karlsson’s June 2021 article distinguished moderate-to-high cardinality from extreme cardinality: it described better query partitioning but slower archival, and warned that unique _id partitions could hurt non-point queries. This is historical advice from the 2021 article. (low confidence)
